solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show embarrassment with the Irish dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blushes while watching a troupe of Irish dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' is the anagram signal, not part of the scene; 'with' supplies its usual one-letter abbreviation at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm or twist about is a physical way of showing acute discomfort, so to show embarrassment is to squirm.

clue.text: Court lacks order in Chancellor's office

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A court of law is short of proper order in the Chancellor's department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges LACKS into LSACK. The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed seat in the House of Lords, formerly the Lord Chancellor's.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat traditionally occupied by the Lord Chancellor stands for that office, as a throne stands for monarchy.

clue.text: Gilbert's fairy tale in Ohio is rewritten

indicators.note: a text that is rewritten has its letters set down in a new arrangement

parts.note: OH is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A Gilbert fairy story is adapted for an American setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rewritten' is the anagram signal. Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera is named after its fairy heroine, so 'Gilbert's fairy' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta is a fairy banished for marrying a mortal.

clue.text: They speed regularly as a stunt

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of these words

explanation.surface: Racers drive fast as a publicity stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of THEY SPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicity stunt is a piece of exaggerated promotion, the same thing as promotional ballyhoo.

clue.text: Orcadian for instance is given heavy blow

parts.note: a lander is slang for a heavy punch that lands

explanation.surface: A man from Orkney takes a hard punch.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orcadian is a native of Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Orkney lives on an island, so is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Trouble with US man behaving badly can be overcome

indicators.note: letters behaving badly are out of line, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American misbehaving causes difficulties, but these can be dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behaving badly' rearranges TROUBLE plus USMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be surmounted is capable of being overcome, like an obstacle climbed over.

clue.text: Last bits of paella will always go further

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the following four words is taken

explanation.surface: The scraped-up leftovers of a paella can always be stretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bits of' takes A, L, S, O from paella, will, always, go.
explanation.definitionFit: Further, used as an adverb of addition, means in addition or besides.

clue.text: Engine stops working on American railway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: a machine that stops working dies
EL is the American term for an elevated railway

explanation.surface: A locomotive breaks down on a US line.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is the US elevated railway, as in Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: A compression-ignition motor named after its inventor Rudolf is a common kind of engine.

clue.text: Turner could make a profit

indicators.note: the letters of the word could make a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A Turner painting might sell for a gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges TURNER, the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment's yield or gain is called its return, as in a return on capital.

clue.text: Mixing soil with touches of potash and xanthin produces flowers

indicators.note: mixing the letters together scrambles them into a new order
a light touch of each word takes only its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener blends potash and a yellow pigment into the earth to grow blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touches of' gives P and X; 'Mixing' rearranges SOIL with them.
explanation.definitionFit: These are primula hybrids of cowslip and primrose, so they are yellow spring flowers.

clue.text: Coppers finally caught criminal in search

indicators.note: letters gone criminal are crooked, so they are rearranged
finally takes only the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Police finally nab a crook after a manhunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T; 'criminal' rearranges COPPERS plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search an area for gold or minerals, so the verb means search.

clue.text: In disarray Dutch rivals serve hard taskmasters

indicators.note: letters in disarray are jumbled out of their order

explanation.surface: Netherlands competitors in confusion work for demanding bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In disarray' rearranges D, RIVALS and SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosses who work people relentlessly are compared to overseers of enslaved workers.

clue.text: Chinese organ emitted melodious sounds

definitions.meaning: a Chinese free-reed mouth organ, also called a sheng
past tense of the verb meaning to vocalise music

explanation.surface: A Chinese instrument made sweet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese mouth organ shares its name with the past tense of the verb for voicing a tune.

clue.text: In Grand Prix John goes to mush

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, splitting it open

parts.note: GP abbreviates Grand Prix
john is US slang for a lavatory, like loo

explanation.surface: A driver called John ends up crushed in a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a racing driver's name, but it is US slang for the lavatory; 'In' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloop is informal for any thick sticky semi-liquid substance, the same as a mush.

clue.text: Mock heartless buffoon

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letters

parts.note: a jester is a court buffoon

explanation.surface: Ridicule a clown with no feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle ST out of JESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock is to taunt with scorn, the same as to taunt with rude shouts.

clue.text: Poor Caruso losing fourth film award

indicators.note: a poor version is a bad rendering, so the letters are rearranged
the fourth letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: The great tenor Caruso, out of luck, misses a fourth movie prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing fourth' drops U from CARUSO; 'Poor' rearranges CARSO. Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is nicknamed after a man's name, the best-known prize in cinema.

clue.text: Emperors finally contract severe lung infection

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: SARS stands for severe acute respiratory syndrome

explanation.surface: Rulers eventually catch a dangerous respiratory illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T from contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian rulers held the imperial title derived from Caesar, so they were emperors.

clue.text: Sticking together I chose seven mates in the end to travel around

indicators.note: letters that travel around move from place to place, so they are rearranged
in the end takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller picks seven friends to roam about with in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives S from mates; 'to travel around' rearranges I CHOSE SEVEN plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the quality of holding firmly together, as particles or a team do.

clue.text: Steps around one street for a mile perhaps

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: dance steps make up a dance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone paces about a road for about a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like walking but means a dance; 'around' signals the container. 'perhaps' marks a mile as only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mile is an example of a length measured between two points.

clue.text: Endless trouble-making that is against Spain brings distress

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble-making
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
V abbreviates versus, against
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Constant stirring against Spain causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts O from AGGRO. AGGRO is British slang for aggressive, violent behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause someone grief or resentment, that is to distress them.

clue.text: Could be Jack's winning by a majority in expressing support for group

parts.note: the jack is an example of a playing card, so Jack is a card
a motion carried in a vote wins by a majority, so carrying

explanation.surface: A man called Jack wins a vote and so backs a political group.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack seems a person's name but is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-carrying member holds a membership card, showing committed support for a party or group.

clue.text: Invest fool with empty hope

parts.note: clot is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Putting money into an idiot's scheme only on a vain hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves H and E from hope. Invest here is the old sense of robing someone in office, not putting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to dress them in ceremonial robes, so it means to dress.

clue.text: Special constable's on edge at start of patrol stint

parts.note: SC abbreviates special constable, a volunteer British police officer
a rim is an edge

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer is on edge as a patrol shift begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives P. A special constable is a part-time unpaid police officer in Britain. Stint looks like a noun for a shift but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing or economise, the same as to skimp and save.

clue.text: Office lost power cord

indicators.note: a word that has lost a letter has it removed

parts.note: a place is a post or office held
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: The office lost electricity because of a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes P from PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lace is a thin cord or string used to fasten shoes.

clue.text: Putting length of timber next to middle of foyer is not well-thought-out

parts.note: a sill is a horizontal beam of wood at a window or door

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fitting a wooden beam in the centre of an entrance hall is a poor idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives Y from foyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolish or ill-considered has not been well thought out.

clue.text: Starts to serve time in rat-infested jail

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A prisoner begins a sentence in a filthy prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes S, T, I, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: It's blue they say over the sea to here

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word is pronounced to give the entry

parts.note: the sky is blue, so blue suggests the sky

explanation.surface: A song lyric about a blue sky above the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song, a Scottish folk song, runs 'Over the sea to Skye', the Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish folk song about Bonnie Prince Charlie's escape names this island as the destination over the sea.

clue.text: Alternative advanced Latin exam

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
A abbreviates advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An optional advanced paper in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: A level is the British advanced school exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test such as a viva is an exam held aloud rather than written.

clue.text: Sturdy country fellow takes part in unusual test

indicators.note: one piece takes its place in the other, splitting it
an unusual arrangement of the letters shuffles them

parts.note: hick is slang for a rustic country man

explanation.surface: A burly rural man sits an odd examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the test into TSET, and 'takes part in' sets the rustic inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickset person is heavily built and stocky, the same as burly.

clue.text: Good area for country house

parts.note: a range is an area, as of grazing land

explanation.surface: A fine stretch of land for a manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings, originally a monastery's outlying farm.

clue.text: Drink squash in Eastern Somalia

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: SO is the international code for Somalia
to squash is to press

explanation.surface: A soft drink served in the east of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash looks like the British fruit cordial but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black coffee forced through ground beans is a drink.

clue.text: Tube is located in foc'sle eventually

indicators.note: the answer is found located in the run of letters of the words

explanation.surface: A pipe is eventually found in the ship's forecastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is located in' finds the entry in foc'SLE EVEntually. The foc'sle is the forward crew quarters of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is a tubular covering or casing fitted round a part, so it is a tube.
